# relay-morpheus — staged runs that outlive the session

A staged run has two records. The transcript, which dies with the session, and
the tree, which does not. Everything that matters has to be in the second one
**while the run is still going**, because there is no guarantee you reach the
end to write it down.

## The rule

```
WRITE THE STAGE DOWN BEFORE YOU DISPATCH IT, NOT AFTER IT COMES BACK
```

This is the one thing this skill exists for, and it is the one thing three
isolated baseline runs did not do (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-morpheus.txt`).
All three executed a four-stage plan end to end and left no on-disk record of
progress until the very last write — one left none at all. A session ending
anywhere before that leaves a working tree full of unattributed diff and no way
to tell which stages produced it, which were finished, or what was still
running.

Reading a mid-run tree is **not** this skill's problem. The companion baseline
(`scenario-relay-morpheus-resume.txt`) shows a fresh session doing that correctly
unprompted, against pressure to trust stale checkboxes. Relay adds nothing
there and says nothing about it.

**Violating the letter of this is violating the spirit of it.** "I'll record it
when the stage returns" is the failure, not a variation on it — the stages that
need recording most are the ones that never return.

## Handing a run to another session

Every run gets a short number when it is created, and `init` prints the
sentence that resumes it:

```
hand this to any session:  continue RUN-3
```

That sentence is the whole interface. A fresh session — another machine,
another host, a colleague — needs nothing else: **"continue RUN-3"**. It has no
transcript, so the ledger is what it reads, and the ledger is on disk because
it was written before the work, not after.

```sh
relay-morpheus.sh list          # every run, what is open, and its resume sentence
relay-morpheus.sh resume 3      # everything a session that has never seen it needs
relay-morpheus.sh 3 status      # any command takes the id first
```

`RUN-3`, `run-3` and `3` all resolve to the same run, because whoever types it
next is working from memory of a conversation rather than from a path. With one
run open and no id given, that run is assumed; with two or more, the script
refuses rather than guessing.

## The run file

`.skillator/run-<id>-<slug>.md`, one per run, in the repo. Markdown because a human and any
host both have to read it with no tooling. Git-tracked by default; a repo that
objects can `.gitignore` it and lose only the shared view, not the resume.

```markdown
# RUN-7 — notekeep v2
plan: docs/plans/PLAN-notekeep.md
started: 2026-09-22T09:14Z   updated: 2026-09-22T10:02Z

## Stages
| # | stage | state | owner | heartbeat | landed |
|---|-------|-------|-------|-----------|--------|
| 41 | list --json     | x | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T09:22Z | 3f1a2c9 |
| 42 | tags + --tag    | ~ | build:sonnet | 2026-09-22T10:02Z | - |
| 43 | export          |   | -            | -     | - |
| 44 | README          |   | -            | -     | - |

## In flight
### stage 42 — tags + --tag  (dispatched 09:51)
prompt: |
  Add a `tags` list to each note in notekeep/store.py and a `list --tag <t>`
  filter in notekeep/cli.py. Test both. Do not touch export or the README.
last seen: wrote store.py, tests not yet run.

## Rulings
- 09:38 — stage 41 emits `[]` not `null` for an empty store — the plan does not
  say, JSON consumers expect a list — costs a one-line change if wrong.
```

**States:** `` (pending) · `~` in flight · `x` landed · `!` failed · `?`
parked (chain only: every item waits on a decision) · `>` re-planned (`landed`
names the new stage).
**`landed`** is a commit sha or a path, never a claim. An empty `landed` on an
`x` row is a lie the next session will believe.
**One run, one worktree (F35).** In a git repo with a commit, `init` also
creates the run's own worktree, `<repo>/.skillator/worktrees/RUN-<n>-<slug>`
(git-ignored, inside the repo so dispatched agents may work there), on
branch `run/RUN-<n>-<slug>`, and writes both into the run file's header. Every
stage of the run works and commits **there** - say so in each dispatch prompt -
never in the main checkout, whose index another run may be using. The run
file itself stays in the main checkout's `.skillator/`, whichever worktree
calls the script. `resume` names the worktree and recreates it from its branch
if it is gone. `init --here` (`-Here`) keeps the old one-checkout behaviour.
The run reaches main through its final stage: merge `run/RUN-<n>-<slug>` from
the main checkout, then `git worktree remove <worktree>` and
`git branch -d run/RUN-<n>-<slug>` - nothing removes them for you.
**Leases across runs (F36).** `chain dispatch` leases the stage's `files:` in
one registry per clone (`<git-common-dir>/skillator/leases`); a file another
run's live stage holds refuses the dispatch (`LEASED <path> RUN-m stage s`,
exit 2) and `chain next` shows the stage `IDLE ... leased`. Landing, failing
or re-planning releases; a lease silent past 20 min is taken, with a ruling.
Board edits from a run worktree go through `relay-morpheus.sh board <ID>
<mark>` (`-Mode board -Ticket -Mark`), which writes the main checkout's
`TICKETS.md` under its lock.
**Parallel stages (F37).** `chain next --all` names every stage that can run
now - files disjoint from what is in flight and from each other - capped at 2
below 50 % of the 5-hour window, else 1. A stage that runs beside another works
in its own worktree off the run branch; `chain merge <n>` brings it back (exit
3 on a conflict: the stage fails). [references/chain.md](references/chain.md).
**A marathon of runs (F38).** Runs wait in one queue (`queue-run add|next|
start|pause|done`), run one at a time, and land on main one at a time
(`land <n> --start`, review and bump on the run branch, `land <n> --finish`);
one end batch across runs (`queue --all`), one push per marathon, and an away
flow (`away on|off`) that notifies, waits 30 minutes and moves on - never a
default. [references/marathon.md](references/marathon.md).
**Numbers are serial across the project, not per run.** `init` takes the RUN
id and every stage number from the F21 allocator (`practice/scripts/next-id.sh`,
kinds `RUN` and `S`), which reads every run file in the tree and on every ref
and keeps a counter every worktree of the clone shares — so two worktrees never
both make RUN-4, and a new run's first stage continues after the highest stage
any run has used (RUN-7 above starts at 41). "Stage 42" names one stage in the
whole project. Existing run files are never renumbered.
**Rulings** are appended, never rewritten — see `tasks-sentinels`, which is
where they come from and which writes into this same file.

## The loop

1. **Before dispatch** — add or update the stage row to `~`, write the In-flight
   block with the *exact prompt you are about to send*, stamp the heartbeat.
   Prompt not written down → the agent is not recoverable → do not dispatch.
2. **While it runs** — re-stamp the heartbeat whenever the agent reports. A
   stale heartbeat is the only signal you get that a network drop took it;
   `hooks/relay-morpheus.* orphans` turns that into a list.
3. **When it lands** — commit the stage's work, then set `x` and put the sha in
   `landed`, and delete its In-flight block. In that order: the sha cannot be
   written before the commit exists.
4. **When it fails** — `!`, and leave the In-flight block where it is with the
   failure appended. A failed stage's prompt is the thing you need most.
5. **Never** delete a row. A run file only grows.

Stages that touch the same files do not run at once; independent ones do
(`PRACTICE.md` §4). Either way each gets its row before it gets its agent.

## Resuming

Open `.skillator/run.md`, then check it against the tree — the file is written
before the work, so the last `~` row is a stage that *started*, not one that
finished. `landed` shas are ground truth; anything else is a claim to verify.
Redispatch straight from the stored prompt; the rows are keyed by stage number,
so a redispatch that duplicates work overwrites rather than appends.

Then carry on. A resume does not need permission to continue — see
`grayskull-power` §3, **run to the end**.

## Chaining ticket workflows

When the stages are ticket workflows that start each other — "work every open
ticket in staged workflows, keep going" — the rule above gains a second half:

```
THE NEXT STAGE IS STARTED BY THE LAST ONE'S COMPLETION, AND BY NOTHING
ELSE UNTIL USAGE SAYS SO
```

Two isolated runs (`practice/baselines/scenario-relay-chain*.txt`) dispatched
with no plan on disk, read no usage between stages, named stages by their
content (two runs picked the same name), and started a stage at 84 % of the
5-hour window. So a chain is run **only** by the loop in
[references/chain.md](references/chain.md): every stage `chain plan`ned with
its code and exact prompt before the first dispatch; `chain decide` (on
`usage-watch level`) before every stage, the first included; `chain hold` at 80 % and a `chain wait` listener instead
of a new stage; `mode:` in the run file naming what was actually dispatched.
Read that file before the first `chain` command.

Every chain is a **marathon**: a question only the user can answer is parked
on disk (`park`), the chain goes on with every stage that does not wait on it
(`chain next`), and the queue is asked once, at the end. The six stops are
never parked:

```
A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION -
NEVER AS ONE ITEM OF THE END BATCH
```

Two baseline runs (`scenario-marathon-stop.txt`) left an untracked directory
alone, said its deletion could not be undone, and then asked it as item 2 of 3
beside a format question. Read [references/marathon.md](references/marathon.md)
when a verdict carries `parked`, a stop fires, or `chain next` prints `ASK` or
`UNBLOCK`.

## Scripts

`hooks/relay-morpheus.sh` · `hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1` — the same commands, mirrored per
`PLATFORMS.md`: `init`, `add`, `stage`, `heartbeat`, `status`, `orphans`, and
`chain plan|dispatch|hold|release|wait|status|decide|next|edge`, and the
marathon's `park`, `answer`, `queue`. They are
bookkeeping, not judgement; every one reads or edits `.skillator/run.md` and
nothing else. Run `selftest` on both after touching either.

```sh
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  init plan.md "notekeep v2" "list --json" "tags" "export" "README"
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  add "docs pass"                    # a stage found mid-run; prints 45
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 '~' build:sonnet          # before you dispatch
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  stage 42 x  build:sonnet 3f1a2c9   # after you commit
sh  relay-morpheus.sh  orphans 20                         # who has gone quiet
```

```powershell
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode init  -Plan plan.md -Title "notekeep v2" -Stages "list --json,tags,export,README"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode add   -Title "docs pass"
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State '~' -Owner build:sonnet
relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode stage -N 42 -State x   -Owner build:sonnet -Landed 3f1a2c9
# In a headless or nested run on Windows, call the .sh through the Bash tool:
# the PowerShell tool refuses `& <script>.ps1` and `powershell -File` under any
# allow rule (A91, claude 2.1.280).
```

Add rows with `add`, never by hand: a hand-typed number is the per-run
restart this numbering removed. The scripts find the allocator beside the
installed skills (`<skills>/practice/scripts/`, or `<root>/practice/scripts/`
in a clone or the plugin cache; `RELAY_NEXT_ID` overrides). Without it they
fall back to the old local rule and say so on stderr — numbers then repeat
across worktrees.

Three constraints the pair has to keep, each learned the hard way:

- **Pure ASCII, and the empty cell is `-`, not an em dash.** Windows PowerShell
  5.1 reads a BOM-less script as ANSI and corrupts anything above 126.
- **The run file is LF with no BOM, written to a temp and moved.** Both mirrors
  edit the same file, so one of them flipping encoding rewrites every line in
  the diff; and a kill between truncate and write would empty the only record
  of what was in flight.
- **`-Stages` takes `"a,b,c"` and pending is spelled `pending`.** PowerShell's
  `-File` passes each argument as one literal string and drops empty ones, and
  `-File` is how every hook here invokes it.

### Seeing a run without being told about one

`list` prints every run with its resume sentence, and prints nothing when there
are none, so it is safe as a `SessionStart` hook. With one wired, a session that inherits
a half-finished run sees it in its own context before the user has to remember
to mention it — which is the difference between resuming and starting over.

```json
{ "hooks": { "SessionStart": [ { "hooks": [ {
  "type": "command",
  "command": "powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File \"<SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.ps1\" -Mode list",
  "timeout": 5
} ] } ] } }
```

macOS/Linux: `sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh list`. Forward slashes throughout —
PowerShell accepts them and it removes all backslash-escaping from the JSON.
Other hosts have no equivalent event; there, reading `.skillator/run.md` is the
first thing `resume-cortana` does. `watch-cortana` already drains in-flight
agents at the limit — relay is what it drains *into*, so the two do not overlap.

1	# Chaining ticket workflows — the procedure
2	
3	A chain is a relay run whose stages are ticket workflows, each started by the
4	previous one's completion notification. Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-relay-chain.md`.
5	The commands below are `hooks/relay-morpheus.sh chain …` (PowerShell:
6	`relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode chain -Action … -N …`); `RM` stands for
7	`sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh`, `UW` for
8	`sh <skills>/watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh`. They are page shorthand only:
9	type the full `sh "<path>" …` every time, never `RM=…; $RM …` — Claude Code's
10	permission check refuses a command whose variable it cannot read (seen in the
11	F31 GREEN run).
12	
13	## When it applies
14	
15	The user asks to work the open tickets as a sequence of workflows — "work every
16	open ticket in staged workflows", "keep going on your own", "auto-start the next
17	workflow", "next stage" — or a resume lands on a run file with a `## Chain`
18	section. A board of 1-3 tickets is `tickets-zordon` plain dispatch, not a chain.
19	
20	## Step 1 — plan from the board (main session, before anything is dispatched)
21	
22	```sh
23	grep -nE '^\s*- \[[ ~!]\]' TICKETS.md
24	```
25	
26	1. `[ ]` and `[~]` go in. A `[~]` stamped by another session's tag is skipped
27	   with a ruling. `[>]` is never planned and never re-checked.
28	2. `[!]` rows: read `(blocked: …)`. Names a ticket that is now `[x]`, or a
29	   file/condition the tree satisfies (check the tree, not the text) → flip it
30	   to `[ ]` and put it in a **later** stage than what unblocked it. Otherwise
31	   leave it out and say so. `(blocked: RUN-n Qk)` resolves only when Qk is
32	   `replanned` or `moot` (`RM chain status` shows `## Decisions`).
33	3. Name the files per ticket (ticket text plus one grep). Same-file tickets are
34	   one item or different stages — never two agents in one stage.
35	4. Tier each ticket per seat (`tickets-zordon` table): `A110 deep/build`.
36	5. One stage = one Workflow call, at most six items, ordered by dependency
37	   then age. The last stage is always `verify review bump commit push`, owned
38	   by the main session. A stage that needs another's output gets `--after <n>`.
39	6. A ticket whose spec leaves a user-owned choice open → `RM park` it now
40	   ([marathon.md](marathon.md), Park); it joins no stage until answered.
41	
42	Write every stage to the run file, then plan every work stage with its exact
43	prompt, **before the first dispatch**:
44	
45	```sh
46	RM init TICKETS.md "drain the board" "B2+B3 books" "F2+F5 report, F3 cli" "verify review bump commit push"
47	printf '%s\n' "<the exact per-item prompts the script will send>" > .skillator/chain-66.txt
48	RM chain plan 66 --tickets "B2,B3" --fix build --verify build --files shelf/books.py --prompt-file .skillator/chain-66.txt
49	```
50	
51	`init` printed the run's worktree (`stages work and commit in: ...`): every
52	prompt file says "work and commit in <worktree> (branch run/RUN-<n>-...),
53	never in the main checkout". The final stage merges that branch into main
54	from the main checkout, then removes the worktree and the branch. A `LEASED`
55	refusal (exit 2) means another run's stage holds one of this stage's files:
56	`chain next` lists it `IDLE <n> leased ...`; dispatch something else and come
57	back after that run lands. Ticket boxes are flipped with `RM board <ID> <mark>`
58	- the main checkout's board, under its lock.
59	
60	`chain plan` allocates the 4-character code (`next-id.sh --runs .skillator W`),
61	prefixes it to the stage cell, and appends a block under `## Chain`. It refuses
62	without a prompt file and never reissues a code. Repeat for each work stage;
63	the final main-session stage needs no block. Without a Workflow tool, add
64	`--mode agents`.
65	
66	Print the plan once — stages, codes, tickets, tiers, agent count, tickets left
67	out and why. A request that said "work the board in stages / keep going" is
68	the opt-in; "plan" stops here. No "shall I continue?" afterwards.
69	
70	## Step 2 — dispatch a stage
71	
72	Read usage first — before **every** dispatch, the first one included. A
73	reading the user gave in the prompt counts too; the higher of the two wins:
74	
75	```sh
76	RM chain decide   # HOLD <pct> → step 4 now, dispatch nothing; RELEASE → go on
77	RM chain dispatch 66 --driver @cc-<6 chars of this session id> --owner build:opus
78	```
79	
80	`dispatch` reads usage itself too. It refuses (exit 2) while `hold:` is set,
81	at or over the 5-hour hold without `--override` (the user asked; a ruling),
82	past the 7-day stop without `--confirmed`, while another driver's stamp is
83	under 20 minutes old (`--take` overrides, with a ruling), and on a stage that
84	is not pending or failed. `UNOBSERVABLE` dispatches, with a one-line note on
85	stderr. The checks and the claim are one lock hold: two sessions dispatching
86	one stage get one winner and one exit 2. On success it sets the row `~`,
87	copies the planned prompt verbatim into an In-flight block, and prints the code
88	and the prompt. Then:
89	
90	1. Flip the stage's tickets to `[~]` with the session tag; grep them back.
91	2. Call `Workflow` with the `work-tickets` script shape from `tickets-zordon`;
92	   every fix and verify prompt carries the marathon.md paste-in paragraph,
93	   and the VERDICT schema its `parked` field.
94	   `meta.name: 'chain-<CODE>'`, every agent `label: '<CODE> fix:B2'` /
95	   `'<CODE> verify:B2'`, `args` = the items with tiers. **An F ticket's item is
96	   a `build-jarvis` pass** (F39), not a bare fix agent: its prompt opens with
97	   "Load skillator:build-jarvis" and the ticket, and build-jarvis grades,
98	   designs and builds it - B and A tickets keep the fix/verify shape.
99	3. Edit the In-flight block's `run: -` to the `runId` the tool returned — no
100	   command fills it. The prompt on disk is the truth; the id is a same-session
101	   hint for `resumeFromRunId`.
102	
103	**Several in flight (F37).** `RM chain next --all` prints one `NEXT` line per
104	stage that can start now - its after: stages landed, its files disjoint from
105	every stage in flight and from the others it names, held by no decision and no
106	other run's lease - capped by usage: 2 below 50 % of the 5-hour window, 1 at or
107	above it or unobservable (`RELAY_CHAIN_PARALLEL` overrides). Dispatch each
108	(one dispatch and one Workflow/Agent call per stage). A stage left out says
109	why: `IDLE <n> slots`, `IDLE <n> parallel-files <m>`, `IDLE <n> inflight-files
110	<m>`; dispatch refuses a stage that shares files with one in flight, and one
111	with no `files:` never runs beside anything. A stage dispatched while another
112	is in flight gets its own worktree off the run branch - dispatch says so on
113	stderr and writes `worktree:`/`branch:` into its In-flight block; its prompt
114	must say to work and commit there. Each stage is landed by Step 3 when **its
115	own** notification arrives - the others keep running - and before its `stage x`
116	run `RM chain merge <n>`: it merges the stage branch into the run branch and
117	removes the stage worktree. Exit 3 is a conflict: the merge is aborted, the
118	stage is `!`, and a retry stage is planned on the merged branch. Then
119	`chain next --all` again fills the free slots.
120	`chain next --holds` (A118) prints only the `IDLE <n> Qk <why>` lines and
121	writes nothing - no lease beat, no lock - for readers such as holo-r2d2.
122	
123	`mode:` in the Chain header names what actually ran: `workflow` for a Workflow
124	call, `agents` for Agent fan-out. A run file that says `workflow` while Agents
125	were used is a lie the next session believes — fix it with
126	`RM chain plan … --mode agents` at planning time, or by editing the header.
127	
128	## Step 3 — between stages (the completion notification is the event)
129	
130	Run every line, in order, before the next dispatch:
131	
132	1. Read the returned array; read `<transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl` before
133	   believing an empty one. `null` → ticket stays `[~]`, said in the ruling.
134	   `passed:false` → `[ ]` with the `why` on the line. `passed:true` → `[x]`
135	   only when the evidence names a check that ran. The main session flips the
136	   board; no agent does. A verdict with `parked` → marathon.md (Park) first:
137	   `RM park` before anything else; `parked.stop` not `none` is a stop, now.
138	2. Regression sweep, then `code-review:code-review` on the staged diff; fix
139	   findings via a fix agent (3-pass cap). Usage pressure lowers the level,
140	   never the call: `/code-review low` is the floor. Reading the diff yourself
141	   is not a review - "to save usage I reviewed it myself" lands nothing.
142	3. Commit with the ticket-first message and the code trailing:
143	   `B2 B3: <what> [<CODE>]`. No review result from step 2, no `x`: the stage
144	   stays `~`. Then `RM stage 66 x build:opus <sha>` and delete
145	   the stage's In-flight block by hand (no command does). No passing ticket →
146	   `RM stage 66 '!'`, block kept with the failure appended, chain continues;
147	   one retry stage per ticket via `RM add`.
148	4. Republish the board artifact once (`tickets-zordon`).
149	5. `Ruling:` line — `<CODE>: <what the verdicts decided, what was dropped>;
150	   review <level>: <n> findings, <fixed|none>`.
151	6. Usage read, every stage, no exception:
152	
153	   ```sh
154	   UW level        # src=<claude-code|codex|none> 5h=<pct|-> 7d=<pct|-> ctx=<pct|-> max=<pct|->
155	   RM chain decide # RELEASE <pct> | HOLD <pct> | HOLD <pct> 7d | UNOBSERVABLE
156	   ```
157	
158	   `HOLD … 7d` → stop #4: `watch-cortana`'s 7-day order runs, and the hold is
159	   also written (step 4 below) so a resume knows why. `HOLD <pct>` → step 4.
160	   `UNOBSERVABLE` → say "usage: unobservable on this host" once in the plan,
161	   `usage: unobservable` in each ruling, and continue — no hold is possible.
162	7. Blocked re-check (step 1.2); a newly unblocked ticket → `RM add "<stage>"`,
163	   then `chain plan` it with its own prompt file.
164	8. Re-read the board; dropped or someone-else's `[~]` tickets leave the item
165	   list with a ruling. Then `RM chain next`: `NEXT` → step 2; `HOLD` → step 4;
166	   `ASK` / `UNBLOCK` → [marathon.md](marathon.md) (The end batch, Unblock)
167	   before anything final; `WAIT` → a stage is in flight, wait for its
168	   notification; `BLOCKED` → stages wait on a failed one: retry it (step 3.3)
169	   and close the failed row `>` naming the retry, or report it; `FINAL` → the
170	   main-session stage: review, version bump, commit; the push asks on its own,
171	   after the batch.

173	## Step 4 — the 80 % hold
174	
175	```sh
176	RM chain hold 84 --window 5h --next 67       # writes `hold: <since> 84% 5h next=67`
177	```
178	
179	Write it before arming anything; it is idempotent and keeps the first `since`.
180	Start nothing. On Claude Code arm the listener under the **Monitor** tool:
181	
182	```sh
183	RM chain wait --for 1500                      # --for 540 in a -p / headless run
184	```
185	
186	Exit 0 `RELEASE <pct>` → `RM chain release`, ruling, dispatch `next`.
187	Exit 5 `WAITING` → the arm's cap is spent; re-arm the same command.

# Chaining ticket workflows — the procedure

A chain is a relay run whose stages are ticket workflows, each started by the
previous one's completion notification. Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-relay-chain.md`.
The commands below are `hooks/relay-morpheus.sh chain …` (PowerShell:
`relay-morpheus.ps1 -Mode chain -Action … -N …`); `RM` stands for
`sh <SKILL>/hooks/relay-morpheus.sh`, `UW` for
`sh <skills>/watch-cortana/hooks/usage-watch.sh`. They are page shorthand only:
type the full `sh "<path>" …` every time, never `RM=…; $RM …` — Claude Code's
permission check refuses a command whose variable it cannot read (seen in the
F31 GREEN run).

## When it applies

The user asks to work the open tickets as a sequence of workflows — "work every
open ticket in staged workflows", "keep going on your own", "auto-start the next
workflow", "next stage" — or a resume lands on a run file with a `## Chain`
section. A board of 1-3 tickets is `tickets-zordon` plain dispatch, not a chain.

## Step 1 — plan from the board (main session, before anything is dispatched)

```sh
grep -nE '^\s*- \[[ ~!]\]' TICKETS.md
```

1. `[ ]` and `[~]` go in. A `[~]` stamped by another session's tag is skipped
   with a ruling. `[>]` is never planned and never re-checked.
2. `[!]` rows: read `(blocked: …)`. Names a ticket that is now `[x]`, or a
   file/condition the tree satisfies (check the tree, not the text) → flip it
   to `[ ]` and put it in a **later** stage than what unblocked it. Otherwise
   leave it out and say so. `(blocked: RUN-n Qk)` resolves only when Qk is
   `replanned` or `moot` (`RM chain status` shows `## Decisions`).
3. Name the files per ticket (ticket text plus one grep). Same-file tickets are
   one item or different stages — never two agents in one stage.
4. Tier each ticket per seat (`tickets-zordon` table): `A110 deep/build`.
5. One stage = one Workflow call, at most six items, ordered by dependency
   then age. The last stage is always `verify review bump commit push`, owned
   by the main session. A stage that needs another's output gets `--after <n>`.
6. A ticket whose spec leaves a user-owned choice open → `RM park` it now
   ([marathon.md](marathon.md), Park); it joins no stage until answered.

Write every stage to the run file, then plan every work stage with its exact
prompt, **before the first dispatch**:

```sh
RM init TICKETS.md "drain the board" "B2+B3 books" "F2+F5 report, F3 cli" "verify review bump commit push"
printf '%s\n' "<the exact per-item prompts the script will send>" > .skillator/chain-66.txt
RM chain plan 66 --tickets "B2,B3" --fix build --verify build --files shelf/books.py --prompt-file .skillator/chain-66.txt
```

`init` printed the run's worktree (`stages work and commit in: ...`): every
prompt file says "work and commit in <worktree> (branch run/RUN-<n>-...),
never in the main checkout". The final stage merges that branch into main
from the main checkout, then removes the worktree and the branch. A `LEASED`
refusal (exit 2) means another run's stage holds one of this stage's files:
`chain next` lists it `IDLE <n> leased ...`; dispatch something else and come
back after that run lands. Ticket boxes are flipped with `RM board <ID> <mark>`
- the main checkout's board, under its lock.

`chain plan` allocates the 4-character code (`next-id.sh --runs .skillator W`),
prefixes it to the stage cell, and appends a block under `## Chain`. It refuses
without a prompt file and never reissues a code. Repeat for each work stage;
the final main-session stage needs no block. Without a Workflow tool, add
`--mode agents`.

Print the plan once — stages, codes, tickets, tiers, agent count, tickets left
out and why. A request that said "work the board in stages / keep going" is
the opt-in; "plan" stops here. No "shall I continue?" afterwards.

## Step 2 — dispatch a stage

Read usage first — before **every** dispatch, the first one included. A
reading the user gave in the prompt counts too; the higher of the two wins:

```sh
RM chain decide   # HOLD <pct> → step 4 now, dispatch nothing; RELEASE → go on
RM chain dispatch 66 --driver @cc-<6 chars of this session id> --owner build:opus
```

`dispatch` reads usage itself too. It refuses (exit 2) while `hold:` is set,
at or over the 5-hour hold without `--override` (the user asked; a ruling),
past the 7-day stop without `--confirmed`, while another driver's stamp is
under 20 minutes old (`--take` overrides, with a ruling), and on a stage that
is not pending or failed. `UNOBSERVABLE` dispatches, with a one-line note on
stderr. The checks and the claim are one lock hold: two sessions dispatching
one stage get one winner and one exit 2. On success it sets the row `~`,
copies the planned prompt verbatim into an In-flight block, and prints the code
and the prompt. Then:

1. Flip the stage's tickets to `[~]` with the session tag; grep them back.
2. Call `Workflow` with the `work-tickets` script shape from `tickets-zordon`;
   every fix and verify prompt carries the marathon.md paste-in paragraph,
   and the VERDICT schema its `parked` field.
   `meta.name: 'chain-<CODE>'`, every agent `label: '<CODE> fix:B2'` /
   `'<CODE> verify:B2'`, `args` = the items with tiers. **An F ticket's item is
   a `build-jarvis` pass** (F39), not a bare fix agent: its prompt opens with
   "Load skillator:build-jarvis" and the ticket, and build-jarvis grades,
   designs and builds it - B and A tickets keep the fix/verify shape.
3. Edit the In-flight block's `run: -` to the `runId` the tool returned — no
   command fills it. The prompt on disk is the truth; the id is a same-session
   hint for `resumeFromRunId`.

**Several in flight (F37).** `RM chain next --all` prints one `NEXT` line per
stage that can start now - its after: stages landed, its files disjoint from
every stage in flight and from the others it names, held by no decision and no
other run's lease - capped by usage: 2 below 50 % of the 5-hour window, 1 at or
above it or unobservable (`RELAY_CHAIN_PARALLEL` overrides). Dispatch each
(one dispatch and one Workflow/Agent call per stage). A stage left out says
why: `IDLE <n> slots`, `IDLE <n> parallel-files <m>`, `IDLE <n> inflight-files
<m>`; dispatch refuses a stage that shares files with one in flight, and one
with no `files:` never runs beside anything. A stage dispatched while another
is in flight gets its own worktree off the run branch - dispatch says so on
stderr and writes `worktree:`/`branch:` into its In-flight block; its prompt
must say to work and commit there. Each stage is landed by Step 3 when **its
own** notification arrives - the others keep running - and before its `stage x`
run `RM chain merge <n>`: it merges the stage branch into the run branch and
removes the stage worktree. Exit 3 is a conflict: the merge is aborted, the
stage is `!`, and a retry stage is planned on the merged branch. Then
`chain next --all` again fills the free slots.
`chain next --holds` (A118) prints only the `IDLE <n> Qk <why>` lines and
writes nothing - no lease beat, no lock - for readers such as holo-r2d2.

`mode:` in the Chain header names what actually ran: `workflow` for a Workflow
call, `agents` for Agent fan-out. A run file that says `workflow` while Agents
were used is a lie the next session believes — fix it with
`RM chain plan … --mode agents` at planning time, or by editing the header.

## Step 3 — between stages (the completion notification is the event)

Run every line, in order, before the next dispatch:

1. Read the returned array; read `<transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl` before
   believing an empty one. `null` → ticket stays `[~]`, said in the ruling.
   `passed:false` → `[ ]` with the `why` on the line. `passed:true` → `[x]`
   only when the evidence names a check that ran. The main session flips the
   board; no agent does. A verdict with `parked` → marathon.md (Park) first:
   `RM park` before anything else; `parked.stop` not `none` is a stop, now.
2. Regression sweep, then `code-review:code-review` on the staged diff; fix
   findings via a fix agent (3-pass cap). Usage pressure lowers the level,
   never the call: `/code-review low` is the floor. Reading the diff yourself
   is not a review - "to save usage I reviewed it myself" lands nothing.
3. Commit with the ticket-first message and the code trailing:
   `B2 B3: <what> [<CODE>]`. No review result from step 2, no `x`: the stage
   stays `~`. Then `RM stage 66 x build:opus <sha>` and delete
   the stage's In-flight block by hand (no command does). No passing ticket →
   `RM stage 66 '!'`, block kept with the failure appended, chain continues;
   one retry stage per ticket via `RM add`.
4. Republish the board artifact once (`tickets-zordon`).
5. `Ruling:` line — `<CODE>: <what the verdicts decided, what was dropped>;
   review <level>: <n> findings, <fixed|none>`.
6. Usage read, every stage, no exception:

   ```sh
   UW level        # src=<claude-code|codex|none> 5h=<pct|-> 7d=<pct|-> ctx=<pct|-> max=<pct|->
   RM chain decide # RELEASE <pct> | HOLD <pct> | HOLD <pct> 7d | UNOBSERVABLE
   ```

   `HOLD … 7d` → stop #4: `watch-cortana`'s 7-day order runs, and the hold is
   also written (step 4 below) so a resume knows why. `HOLD <pct>` → step 4.
   `UNOBSERVABLE` → say "usage: unobservable on this host" once in the plan,
   `usage: unobservable` in each ruling, and continue — no hold is possible.
7. Blocked re-check (step 1.2); a newly unblocked ticket → `RM add "<stage>"`,
   then `chain plan` it with its own prompt file.
8. Re-read the board; dropped or someone-else's `[~]` tickets leave the item
   list with a ruling. Then `RM chain next`: `NEXT` → step 2; `HOLD` → step 4;
   `ASK` / `UNBLOCK` → [marathon.md](marathon.md) (The end batch, Unblock)
   before anything final; `WAIT` → a stage is in flight, wait for its
   notification; `BLOCKED` → stages wait on a failed one: retry it (step 3.3)
   and close the failed row `>` naming the retry, or report it; `FINAL` → the
   main-session stage: review, version bump, commit; the push asks on its own,
   after the batch.

## Step 4 — the 80 % hold

```sh
RM chain hold 84 --window 5h --next 67       # writes `hold: <since> 84% 5h next=67`
```

Write it before arming anything; it is idempotent and keeps the first `since`.
Start nothing. On Claude Code arm the listener under the **Monitor** tool:

```sh
RM chain wait --for 1500                      # --for 540 in a -p / headless run
```

Exit 0 `RELEASE <pct>` → `RM chain release`, ruling, dispatch `next`.
Exit 5 `WAITING` → the arm's cap is spent; re-arm the same command.
Exit 3 `STUCK` → ruling, one more arm, then `AskUserQuestion` with the reading.
Exit 4 `UNOBSERVABLE` → release; the hold should never have been written.
Exit 2 `STOP <pct> 7d` → the 7-day window, not the 5-hour one: it will not refill
while you wait. Stop #4 — TaskStop the Monitor and hand off; a dispatch past it
needs `--confirmed`, never `--override`.
Hosts without Monitor record the hold, say "held at 84 %; say *next stage*, or
`continue RUN-<n>` later", and end the turn.

The hold is a wait, not a stop: no session handoff is written for it (that is
`watch-cortana`'s 92 % order). The threshold is `RELAY_CHAIN_HOLD_PCT` (80).

## Override — "next stage", "go on", "don't wait" while held

```sh
UW level
RM chain release --override                   # refused with exit 2 past 7d 90 %
```

Under the 7-day stop: TaskStop the Monitor, ruling `override: user asked at
<pct>%` (the command writes it), then `RM chain dispatch <n> … --override` —
dispatch re-reads usage, and the reading is still over 80 %. At or over 7-day 90 %:
`AskUserQuestion` — "7-day window at 91 % — the hard stop. Start <CODE>
anyway?" with *Hold (recommended — the window does not refill for days)* first.
Only the explicit yes runs `RM chain release --override --confirmed` and
`RM chain dispatch <n> … --confirmed`.

## Crash and resume

`RM list` (the SessionStart hook) names the run; `RM resume <id>` prints the
whole file, `## Chain` included. A `~` row is a stage that *started*: check the
tree, then redispatch from the In-flight prompt (or `resumeFromRunId` when the
id is this session's). `hold:` set → `UW level`; under → `RM chain release` and
dispatch `next`; over → `RM chain hold` again (same `since`) and arm the
listener. The driver's stamp is refreshed by its own `dispatch`, `heartbeat`,
`hold`, `release` and every `wait` poll, so a tag older than 20 minutes is a
driver that stopped, and may be taken.
Nothing is asked but the parked queue (`chain next` → `ASK`); the file is the plan.

1	# Marathon — park the user's questions, ask them all at the end
2	
3	Every chain runs as a marathon unless the user said "ask me as you go"
4	(`RM queue --asks live`, then a parked question is asked at the next
5	between-stage point). Design: `docs/plans/PLAN-marathon.md`. `RM` is the same
6	page shorthand as in [chain.md](chain.md): type the full `sh "<path>" …` every
7	time. PowerShell: `-Mode park|answer|queue`, `-Mode chain -Action next|edge`.
8	
9	## Stops — never parked, asked now and alone
10	
11	```
12	A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION.
13	IT IS NEVER AN ITEM IN THE END BATCH.
14	```
15	
16	The six grayskull stops: a destructive or irreversible op, a security-sensitive
17	action, a side effect outside the worktree (push, merge, publish, message), the
18	7-day window at 90 %, a scope-contract breach, a failed repro. When one fires:
19	dispatch nothing new, end your message with that one question — what the act is,
20	that it cannot be undone, *Hold (recommended)* first — and nothing else in it.
21	The open queue is offered **after** the user has answered the stop, never beside
22	it. Two baseline runs saw that deleting untracked `data/legacy/` could not be
23	undone, said so, and still listed it as item 2 of 3 next to a format question:
24	a destructive op approved as one line of a batch is a rubber stamp. That is the
25	failure. "It's all questions for the same user" does not make a stop a decision;
26	`park` refuses `--stop` other than `none` (exit 2).
27	
28	Stops 5 and 6 are item-level by default (F31: the ticket fails `passed:false`,
29	never parked). The whole chain stops only when that ticket has dependants
30	(`after:`, `blocks:`, held files) or two repros fail in a row. The chain's own
31	push stays last, asked on its own after the unblock rounds.
32	
33	## Park — only what the user alone can decide
34	
35	All four, or it is a `Ruling:` with the default, as today:
36	1. **reason** `taste` (preference nothing settles), `fact` (only the user knows —
37	   *where* a credential lives, never its value) or `conflict` (ticket, spec and
38	   the user's words disagree and none binds);
39	2. not a stop;
40	3. two to four real options;
41	4. a default a ruling would pick.
42	
43	A park is the question written down **before** the next dispatch: park (disk) →
44	board flip (`[!] (blocked: RUN-n Qk - <8 words>)`, or split `F2a` done / `F2b`
45	blocked) → commit what passed → `RM stage <n> x|?` → ruling → `RM chain next`.

49	  --question "Should export write CSV or JSON by default?" --header Format \
50	  --option "JSON | matches list --json | breaks the spreadsheet habit" \
51	  --option "CSV | opens in Excel | needs a quoting rule" \
52	  --default JSON --recommended JSON --blocks "F2b, F5" \
53	  --files "shelf/export.py, tests/test_export.py" --done "F2a landed in AAQ7" --stop none
54	```
55	
56	It prints `Q<k>` (always quote it with the run: `RUN-11 Q2`). Planning-time

58	Q and writes nothing, so replaying step 3 after a crash is safe. `park` refuses

A STOP IS ASKED THE MOMENT IT IS REACHED, AS THE ONLY QUESTION.
IT IS NEVER AN ITEM IN THE END BATCH.
```

action, a side effect outside the worktree (push, merge, publish, message), the
7-day window at 90 %, a scope-contract breach, a failed repro. When one fires:
dispatch nothing new, end your message with that one question — what the act is,
that it cannot be undone, *Hold (recommended)* first — and nothing else in it.

it. Two baseline runs saw that deleting untracked `data/legacy/` could not be
undone, said so, and still listed it as item 2 of 3 next to a format question:
a destructive op approved as one line of a batch is a rubber stamp. That is the
failure. "It's all questions for the same user" does not make a stop a decision;
`park` refuses `--stop` other than `none` (exit 2).

"""The catalogue, in memory."""
_BOOKS = []


def add(title, author):
    book = {"title": title, "author": author}
    _BOOKS.append(book)
    return book


def find(query):
    return [b for b in _BOOKS if query in b["title"]]


def all_books():
    return list(_BOOKS)


def clear():
    _BOOKS.clear()
import argparse

from shelf import books, report


def main(argv=None):
    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="shelf")
    sub = p.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    a = sub.add_parser("add")
    a.add_argument("title")
    a.add_argument("author")
    f = sub.add_parser("find")
    f.add_argument("query")
    sub.add_parser("report")
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "add":
        books.add(args.title, args.author)
    elif args.cmd == "find":
        for b in books.find(args.query):
            print("%s - %s" % (b["title"], b["author"]))
    else:
        print(report.summary())
    return 0

content.text:
# Workflow authoring reference

A workflow structures work across many agents — to be comprehensive (decompose and cover in parallel), to be confident (independent perspectives and adversarial checks before committing), or to take on scale one context can't hold (migrations, audits, broad sweeps). The script is where you encode that structure: what fans out, what verifies, what synthesizes.

When you do call it, the right move is often **hybrid**: scout inline first (list the files, find the channels, scope the diff) to discover the work-list, then call Workflow to pipeline over it. You don't need to know the shape before the *task* — only before the *orchestration step*.

Common single-phase workflows you can chain across turns:
- **Understand** — parallel readers over relevant subsystems → structured map
- **Design** — judge panel of N independent approaches → scored synthesis
- **Review** — dimensions → find → adversarially verify (the review-changes example)
- **Research** — multi-modal sweep → deep-read → synthesize
- **Migrate** — discover sites → transform each (worktree isolation) → verify

For larger work, run several in sequence — read each result before deciding the next phase. You stay in the loop; each workflow is one well-scoped fan-out.

**Ultracode.** When a system-reminder confirms ultracode is on, that opt-in is standing: author and run a workflow for every substantive task by default. The goal is the most exhaustive, correct answer you can produce — token cost is not a constraint. For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:

- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")

  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)

    bugs.push(...result.bugs)

  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.
